questions.question: Which of the following options is correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The pair Decomposers – Bacteria is correctly matched.
  • Decomposers (like bacteria and fungi) break down dead organic matter into simpler inorganic substances.
  • Green plants are Autotrophs/Producers, not omnivores.
  • Primary consumers are Herbivores, while Secondary consumers are typically Carnivores.

questions.question: Which is an integral membrane protein that forms the tetramer and facilitates the diffusion of water and some small, unmodified solutes across cellular membranes?
questions.solution:
Aquaporins are integral membrane proteins that act as 'plumbing systems' for cells.
  • They form a tetramer (four-part structure) in the cell membrane to facilitate the rapid diffusion of water.
  • They are highly selective, allowing water molecules to pass through while preventing the passage of ions and other solutes.

questions.question: Identify the organelle present in plant cell that is not there in an animal cell.
questions.solution:
Plastids (such as Chloroplasts) are organelles found in plant cells but are entirely absent in animal cells.
  • They are responsible for photosynthesis and the storage of starches or pigments.
  • Note: Neurons are a type of cell, not an organelle, and both animal and plant cells possess a nucleus and cytoplasm.

questions.question: What is the fourth step in mitosis where non-kinetochore spindle fibres lengthen and elongate the cell?
questions.solution:
During Anaphase, the fourth stage of mitosis, sister chromatids separate toward opposite poles while non-kinetochore spindle fibers lengthen to elongate the cell.
  • This elongation prepares the cell for the final physical split during cytokinesis.

questions.question: Which Greek term was first used by Ernst Haeckel in 1866 to refer to ‘the relation of animals to both the organic as well as the inorganic environment’?
questions.solution:
The Greek term Oekologie (Ecology) was first coined by Ernst Haeckel in 1866.
  • He defined it as the study of the relationship between an organism and its environment.
  • The term is derived from the Greek words 'Oikos' (house) and 'Logos' (study).

questions.question: Who described the algae Spirogyra in 1674 and named the motile organisms Animalcules, meaning ‘little animals’?
questions.solution:
Anton Van Leeuwenhoek, often called the 'Father of Microbiology,' described Spirogyra and discovered motile microorganisms he called Animalcules.
  • In 1674, using his handcrafted lenses, he became the first person to observe bacteria and protozoa in a drop of pond water.

questions.question: Identify the largest phylum in the animal kingdom.
questions.solution:
Arthropoda is the largest phylum in the animal kingdom, comprising over 80% of all known living animal species.
  • It includes insects, spiders, crabs, and scorpions.
  • Key features include jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton.

questions.question: Which protein is found in grains?
questions.solution:
Gluten is the main structural protein found in grains such as wheat, barley, and rye.
  • It provides elasticity to dough, helping it rise and keep its shape.
  • Note: Arginine is an amino acid, not a specific grain protein.

questions.question: Which of the following foods generally increase blood pressure?
questions.option_3: Food high in salt, sugar and saturated or trans fats
questions.option_4: Food with low salt and low sugar
questions.solution:
Diets high in salt (sodium), sugar, and saturated or trans fats are primary contributors to increased blood pressure (hypertension).
  • High salt intake causes the body to retain water, putting extra pressure on blood vessel walls.
  • Fibre and low-salt diets generally help lower or stabilize blood pressure.

questions.question: Garlic is good source of:
questions.solution:
Garlic is particularly high in essential trace minerals like manganese and selenium.
  • These minerals contribute to its antioxidant properties and its reputation for supporting heart health and the immune system.

questions.question: Which vitamin is involved in red blood cell formation, neurological function and DNA synthesis?
questions.solution:
Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin) is essential for red blood cell formation, healthy neurological function, and DNA synthesis.
  • A deficiency in B12 can lead to pernicious anemia and nerve damage.
  • It is naturally found in animal products like meat, fish, and dairy.

questions.question: What are the thin filamentous extensions that the motile bacterial cells have from their cell wall called?
questions.solution:
Flagella are the thin, filamentous extensions from the cell wall that provide motility to bacterial cells.
  • Distinction: Pili and Fimbriae are also surface appendages but are primarily used for attachment (adhesion) or genetic exchange, not swimming.

questions.question: Which bacteria have a thick cell wall with several layers of peptidoglycan and teichoic acid?
questions.solution:
Staphylococcus aureus is a Gram-positive bacterium, meaning it has a thick cell wall composed of many layers of peptidoglycan and teichoic acid.
  • E. coli and Salmonella are Gram-negative and have much thinner peptidoglycan layers but an outer membrane.

questions.question: Identify the reason for formation of dental plaque.
questions.option_1: Masses of bacterial cells together with food particles stick to the teeth
questions.option_3: When bacteria acting on sugars produce acids
questions.option_4: When acids stick to the teeth
questions.solution:
Dental plaque forms when masses of bacterial cells and food particles stick to the surface of the teeth.
  • If not removed, the bacteria process sugars into acids, which eventually demineralize the enamel and cause cavities.

questions.question: Identify a mobile source of food.
questions.solution:
A Deer is a mobile source of food because it is a living organism that moves within its ecosystem.
  • For a predator, mobile food requires active hunting or pursuit, unlike stationary sources like grass or shrubs.

questions.question: Identify an organelle found both in eukaryotic as well as prokaryotic.
questions.solution:
Ribosomes are the protein-synthesizing 'factories' found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
  • Prokaryotes have 70S ribosomes, while Eukaryotes have 80S ribosomes (in the cytoplasm).
  • Note: Mitochondria and Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles found only in Eukaryotes.

questions.question: What is a population (or subspecies or race) that is adapted to local environmental conditions called?
questions.solution:
An Ecotype is a genetically distinct geographic variety or population within a species, which is adapted to specific local environmental conditions.
  • While they look different, different ecotypes of the same species can still interbreed.

questions.question: Identify a muscle responsible for exit of waste material from the body.
questions.solution:
An anal sphincter is a ring of muscle responsible for controlling the exit of waste material (feces) from the body.
  • Sphincters act as valves throughout the digestive system to ensure the one-way flow of material.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms can initiate ecological succession even in bare rocks?
questions.solution:
Lichens are 'pioneer species' that can initiate ecological succession on bare rocks.
  • They secrete acids that break down the rock into soil, paving the way for mosses and eventually larger plants to grow.

questions.question: Identify the organism that shows bioluminescence.
questions.solution:
Ctenoplana belongs to the phylum Ctenophora (comb jellies), which are well-known for their ability to show bioluminescence (emitting light).
  • This light is often used to attract prey or distract predators in the deep ocean.

questions.question: Identify the structure that controls the size of the pupil.
questions.solution:
The Iris is the colored part of the eye that controls the size of the pupil.
  • By contracting or relaxing, the iris regulates the amount of light entering the eye.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in the Indian Food Guide Pyramid for healthy eating?
questions.solution:
Alcoholic beverages are not included in the Indian Food Guide Pyramid, which focuses on nutrient-dense food groups like cereals, pulses, milk, and fats.
  • The pyramid is designed to promote a balanced diet for health and disease prevention.

questions.question: To what phylum does a blood sucking leech belong?
questions.solution:
The blood-sucking leech belongs to the phylum Annelida.
  • Annelids are characterized by segmented bodies.
  • Leeches specifically belong to the class Hirudinea.

questions.question: Which hairpin-like structure serves to anchor and stabilise the tick's mouthparts to its host's skin and to channel the exchange of fluids?
questions.solution:
The Hypostome is a calcified, harpoon-like structure near the mouth of a tick.
  • It allows the tick to anchor itself firmly into the host's skin while it feeds on blood.

questions.question: The body of the phylum ________ is unsegmented and dorsoventrally flattened.
questions.solution:
The phylum Platyhelminthes (Flatworms) is characterized by a body that is unsegmented and dorsoventrally flattened.
  • They are Acoelomates, meaning they lack a body cavity between the gut and the outer body wall.

questions.question: What is the shape of the eyeball?
questions.solution:
The human eyeball is approximately spherical in shape.
  • It has a diameter of about 2.3 cm.
  • The spherical shape allows it to rotate easily within the eye socket (orbit) using the extraocular muscles.
